small_sample_uncertainty.interpretation: With only 5 true exoplanets in the test set, each individual example represents 20.0% of the recall metric. An observed recall of 20.0% corresponds to a wide 95% Wilson confidence interval of [3.6%, 62.4%]. Reported test recall inherently exhibits significant small-sample statistical uncertainty.

test_evaluation_selected_threshold_0_08.imbalance_explanation: The test dataset is severely imbalanced (565 non-exoplanets vs 5 confirmed exoplanets, representing ~99.12% vs ~0.88%). A naive majority-class classifier that blindly predicts class 1 for all samples achieves an accuracy of 99.12%, yet completely fails to detect a single exoplanet (0% recall on class 2). Therefore, accuracy alone is misleading; recall and F1-score for the positive minority class (class 2) are the primary indicators of transit detection efficacy.
test_evaluation_selected_threshold_0_08.domain_interpretation_disclaimer: TransitHunter AI predicts the classes represented by its training dataset labels (1: non-exoplanet, 2: confirmed exoplanet). A positive prediction indicates statistical similarity to confirmed Kepler transit flux patterns, but does not constitute physical or astronomical proof that an unknown star hosts an exoplanet.
